explanation: A struct in C is a user-defined data type that groups together variables of different types under a single name. It is used to model real-world entities or concepts, such as a disk drive, by organizing related data into a single unit, making code more readable and easier to manage.
syntax: struct StructName { type member1; type member2; };
example_explanation: This example defines a struct named Disk to represent a disk with capacity and speed attributes, mirroring the idea of a functional model. It creates an instance of the struct, assigns values to its members, and prints them, showing how structs group and access related data to model a concept like a disk drive.
